test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 6 March 2023)
subject: general
question: The difference between the length of two parallel sides of a trapezium is 12 cm. The perpendicular distance between these two parallel sides is 60 cm. If the area of the trapezium is 1380 cm², then find the length of each of the parallel sides (in cm).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of parallel sides = (2 × Area) ÷ Height

⇒ Sum = (2 × 1380) ÷ 60 = 46 cm.

Given Difference = 12 cm.

Sides = (Sum ± Difference) ÷ 2 = (46 ± 12) ÷ 2 = 29 cm and 17 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 29, 17 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Area of trapezium = 1380 cm²

Height (h) = 60 cm

Difference between parallel sides (a − b) = 12 cm

Formula used: Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (a + b) × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7012e468670cc0b4411622f8aaed9e8ff7270fd937706b817734e67dc0d9dbe1.png] 

⇒ 1380 = 1/2 × (a + b) × 60

⇒ 1380 = 30 × (a + b)

⇒ a + b = 1380 ÷ 30

⇒ a + b = 46 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ a − b = 12 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding (1) and (2): 2a = 58 ⇒ a = 29 cm

⇒ Substituting in (1): 29 + b = 46 ⇒ b = 17 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 29, 17 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Trapezium

The area is calculated as the product of the average of the parallel sides and the perpendicular distance between them: Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height.

Median of a Trapezium

The median (mid-segment) is parallel to the bases and its length is the average of the bases: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Isosceles Trapezium

A trapezium where the non-parallel sides are equal in length and the base angles are also equal.</p
